blocks.text: **First name the reference group.** P(A | B) asks: among cases in B, what share are also in A? Compute (A and B) / B. B is the denominator; the whole sample is not.

blocks.setup: Practice A Q1: 40 students; 25 commute; 10 of the commuters cycle. Let B = commuters and A = cyclists.

steps.label: Reference group
steps.text: B = the 25 commuters (the question asks what share of commuters cycle).

steps.label: Two-way table
steps.text: A row percentage divides its cell by that row total; a column percentage divides its cell by that column total. Pick the total for the group named in the question.

blocks.takeaway: Report proportions as a percentage rounded to one decimal place, and name the reference group in words. The order matters: P(A | B) and P(B | A) usually differ. (Outline reporting rule; Notes §§1.1–1.4, 2.2; Practice A Q1)

blocks.text: Within each row, row percentages sum to 100%; within each column, column percentages sum to 100%. Across a row of column percentages, totals need not be 100%. (Notes §2.3)

Split cases by a categorical variable; compute one summary (such as a mean or count) for each non-empty group. Output: one row per group, not per original case. Compare groups using the same summary (mean with mean, count with count). (Notes §§3.1–3.3)
